## Import Data

```{r}
# Load packages 
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(spData)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(units)
library(geosphere)
```

## Data

```{r}
# Read in three excel files from MARINe biodiversity data 
point_contact_raw <- read_excel(here('data', 'MARINe_biodiversity_data',
                                     'cbs_data_CA_2023.xlsx'), sheet = 'point_contact_summary_data')
quadrat_raw <- read_excel(here('data', 'MARINe_biodiversity_data',
                               'cbs_data_CA_2023.xlsx'), sheet = 'quadrat_summary_data')
swath_raw <- read_excel(here('data', 'MARINe_biodiversity_data',
                             'cbs_data_CA_2023.xlsx'), sheet = 'swath_summary_data')

# Read in Dangermond preserve shape file 
dangermond <- read_sf(here('data', 'dangermond_shapefile', 'jldp_boundary.shp'))
CA_coastline_shp <- read_sf(here('data', 'coastal_spatial_data',
                                 'coast.line.CA.shp'))
# Read in California state boundary 
california <- spData::us_states %>% 
  filter(NAME == "California")

# Add southern and northern bounds of california
coastline_segments <- read_csv(here::here("data", "coastal_spatial_data",
                                 "coast.CA.100km.chunks.csv")) %>% 
    rename(lat = Y, long = X) %>% 
    st_as_sf(coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = st_crs(dangermond), remove = FALSE) %>% 
    mutate(segment_id = 1:nrow(.))
```

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
# Clean point_contact dataset 
point_contact_clean <- point_contact_raw %>% 
  # Remove non-matching columns 
  select(!c('number_of_transect_locations', 'percent_cover')) %>% 
  # Rename num of hits to total count 
  rename(total_count = number_of_hits) %>% 
  # Create new data collection source column 
  mutate(collection_source = "point contact") %>% 
  # Filter to mainland only 
  filter(island == "Mainland") %>% 
  # Remove certain species lumps 
  filter(!species_lump %in% c("Rock", "Sand", "Tar", "Blue Green Algae", "Red Crust", "Diatom", "Ceramiales"))

# Clean quadrat dataset 
quadrat_clean <- quadrat_raw %>% 
  # Remove non-matching columns 
  select(!c('number_of_quadrats_sampled', 'total_area_sampled_m2', 'density_per_m2')) %>% 
  # Create new data collection source column 
  mutate(collection_source = "quadrat") %>% 
  # Filter to mainland only 
  filter(island == "Mainland") %>% 
  # Remove certain species lumps 
  filter(!species_lump %in% c("Rock", "Sand", "Tar", "Blue Green Algae", "Red Crust", "Diatom", "Ceramiales"))

# Clean swath dataset 
swath_clean <- swath_raw %>% 
  # Remove non-matching columns 
  select(!c('number_of_transects_sampled', 'est_swath_area_searched_m2',  'density_per_m2')) %>% 
  # Create new data collection source column 
  mutate(collection_source = "swath") %>% 
  # Filter to mainland only 
  filter(island == "Mainland") %>% 
  # Remove certain species lumps 
  filter(!species_lump %in% c("Rock", "Sand", "Tar", "Blue Green Algae", "Red Crust", "Diatom", "Ceramiales"))
```

```{r}
# Merge datasets
biodiv_merge <- bind_rows(point_contact_clean, quadrat_clean, swath_clean)
```

```{r}
# Group by site and species
biodiv_total <- biodiv_merge %>% 
  group_by(marine_site_name, latitude, longitude, species_lump, year) %>% 
  summarise(num_count = sum(total_count), .groups = 'drop') %>% 
  mutate(presence = ifelse(num_count >= 1, 1, 0))
```

#### Convert biodiv data to sf object

```{r}
biodiv_geo <- biodiv_total %>% 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = st_crs(CA_coastline_shp), remove = FALSE)

# Check that the crs matches 
if(st_crs(CA_coastline_shp) == st_crs(biodiv_geo)) {
  print("The coordinate reference systems match")
} else {
  print("The coordinate reference systems do NOT match. Transformation of CRS is recommended.")
}

```
```{r}

# 5. Create LineSegments from coastal points in the CA coastline
# Assuming 'CA_coastline_shp' has 'geometry' column as coordinates (longitude, latitude)

# Create a LineString from each consecutive pair of points along the coastline
coastline_coords <- st_coordinates(CA_coastline_shp)
line_segments <- list()

for (i in 1:(nrow(coastline_coords) - 1)) {
  line_segments[[i]] <- st_sfc(st_linestring(matrix(c(coastline_coords[i, 1], coastline_coords[i, 2], 
                                                     coastline_coords[i + 1, 1], coastline_coords[i + 1, 2]), 
                                                   ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)), crs = st_crs(CA_coastline_shp))
}

# Convert list of line segments into an sf object
line_segments_sf <- st_sf(geometry = do.call(c, line_segments))

# 6. Create a spatial index for the line segments
line_segments_sf_indexed <- st_as_sf(line_segments_sf)  # Just to ensure it's in sf format
st_is_valid(line_segments_sf_indexed)  # Ensure all geometries are valid

# 7. Use st_intersects to find the marine sites lying within the line segments
# Spatial query: Find the closest segment that intersects with each marine site
biodiv_geo$segment_id <- NA  # Initialize segment_id for marine sites

# 8. Efficient intersection check using spatial operations
for (i in 1:nrow(biodiv_geo)) {
  marine_site <- biodiv_geo[i, , drop = FALSE]  # Single marine site
  # Check which line segments the marine site intersects with
  intersects <- st_intersects(marine_site, line_segments_sf, sparse = FALSE)
  
  if (any(intersects)) {
    biodiv_geo$segment_id[i] <- which(intersects)[1]  # Assign the first segment that intersects
  }
}

# 9. Save the results with the new segment_id
write.csv(biodiv_geo, "biodiv_geo_segments.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# 10. (Optional) View the updated marine_sites data
head(biodiv_geo)

```
